{"kind":"tool","id":"cxDlQv947-g","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"README.md","instructions":"Project README covering setup, local dev and Vercel deployment","content":"# Payvand

A two-sided Solana payment app.

- **Seller** connects a wallet, enters an amount, and the app opens an on-chain
  invoice (`Payment` PDA) with an Anchor program, then renders a QR code.
- **Buyer** scans the code with their camera, sees the amount and memo, and
  approves a `settle_payment` transaction from their own wallet.
- The **Axum API** validates payment requests and reports live on-chain status.
  It is deliberately stateless, so it runs identically as a local process and
  as a serverless function.

## Stack

| Part      | Tech                                                       |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frontend  | Nuxt 4, Nuxt UI v4, Tailwind CSS 4, [@vue-solana/nuxt][vs] |
| QR        | `qrcode` (generate), `jsqr` (camera scan)                  |
| Backend   | Rust, Axum 0.8, `solana-rpc-client`                        |
| Solana    | Anchor 1.1.2 program (`programs/payvand`)                  |
| Hosting   | Vercel (web project + API project)                         |

[vs]: https://vue-solana-docs.vercel.app/packages/nuxt

## Repository layout

```
app/                 Nuxt app (pages, components, composables)
  pages/sell.vue     Seller: create invoice + render QR
  pages/pay.vue      Buyer: scan QR + pay
  assets/payvand.idl.json   Copy of the Anchor IDL used by the client
progr [… 2,211 characters omitted]  web          | `""` (same origin) | Origin of the Axum API in production   |
| `NUXT_PUBLIC_SOLANA_ENDPOINT`   | web          | cluster default | Custom RPC endpoint                       |
| `BIND_ADDR`                     | api          | `127.0.0.1:8787`| Local listen address                      |
| `SOLANA_RPC_URL`                | api          | cluster default | RPC endpoint the API uses for status reads |

Never put a wallet secret key or a seed phrase anywhere in this repository. The
Nuxt module deliberately strips `payer` and `payerSecretKey` from its public
runtime config for the same reason.

## Deploying to Vercel (Hobby plan)

Vercel cannot host both parts in one project, so the repository deploys as **two
Vercel projects** pointing at the same repo. Both work on the Hobby plan.

### 1. Web app

- Import the repo in Vercel with **Root Directory = `.`** (the repo root).
  Vercel detects Nuxt automatically; no `vercel.json` is needed.
- Set `NUXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE` to the origin of the API project below.

### 2. API

- Create a second Vercel project from the same repo with
  **Root Directory = `server`** and Framework Preset = **Other**.
- `server/vercel.json` rewrites every path to the Rust binary
  (`api/axum.rs`), which mounts the same Axum router through
  `vercel_runtime`'s `VercelLayer`. The Rust runtime is currently in beta on
  all plans.
- Redeploy the web project after the API has a URL so it picks up
  `NUXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE`.

The API is stateless: every response is derived from the request and the
chain, so separate serverless isolates never disagree.

## Notes and next steps

- The QR payload is a small JSON blob (`{v,id,seller,reference,amount_lamports,memo,cluster,endpoint}`).
  It is readable by this app only. If you want third-party wallets to be able
  to pay straight from their own scanner, switch the payload to the
  [Solana Pay URL format](https://docs.solanapay.com/spec) — the reference and
  amount fields map one to one.
- Cluster defaults in the API are the public `api.*.solana.com` endpoints. For
  anything beyond testing, set `SOLANA_RPC_URL` to a dedicated provider.
- `settle_payment` moves lamports straight from the payer to the seller; the
  program only records the invoice. `close_payment` lets the seller reclaim the
  rent once it has been settled.

**What's in the repo**

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| [programs/payvand/src/lib.rs](programs/payvand/src/lib.rs) | Anchor 1.1.2 program: `create_payment` (seller opens a `Payment` PDA), `settle_payment` (payer pays, lamports move payer→seller), `close_payment` (reclaim rent) |
| [server/src/lib.rs](server/src/lib.rs) | Axum API — `GET /health`, `POST /api/payments` (validates a request + returns the QR payload), `GET /api/payments/{pda}` (live status read from the cluster) |
| [server/api/axum.rs](server/api/axum.rs) | Same router wrapped in `VercelLayer` for Vercel's Rust runtime |
| [app/pages/sell.vue](app/pages/sell.vue) | Seller: wallet connect → amount/memo → signs `create_payment` → renders the QR |
| [app/pages/pay.vue](app/pages/pay.vue) | Buyer: camera scan (`jsqr`) → invoice details → signs `settle_payment` |
| [app/composables/usePaymentProgram.ts](app/composables/usePaymentProgram.ts) | Builds Anchor instructions straight from the IDL (discriminators + Borsh args + PDA seeds) and compiles them to wire bytes for Kit |
| [nuxt.config.ts](nuxt.config.ts) | `@vue-solana/nuxt`, Nuxt UI, Tailwind, dev proxy `/api` → `:8787` |

I started from the Nuxt `ui` starter template and adapted it. Stack: Nuxt 4.6 + Nuxt UI 4 + Tailwind 4, `@vue-solana/nuxt` 3.0 (per [the docs you linked](https://vue-solana-docs.vercel.app/packages/nuxt)), `qrcode` + `jsqr`, Axum 0.8 + `solana-rpc-client`, Anchor 1.1.2.

**Verified**
- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build` — clean.
- `cargo test` in both workspaces (5 API tests pass), `cargo fmt --check`, `anchor build` → `payvand.so` + IDL + TS types.
- Live: API on `127.0.0.1:8787` reached **devnet** through `solana-rpc-client` and correctly reported `status: "missing"` for an unopened invoice; the dev proxy forwarded `POST /api/payments`; `/`, `/sell`, `/pay` render (browser-verified, no console errors in the production build); pasting a QR payload on `/pay` parsed it, called the API and rendered the invoice card with amount, memo and status.

**Not verified:** an actual on-chain transaction (needs a funded wallet extension), and an actual Vercel deploy — I didn't deploy anything.

**On Vercel:** it can't host both halves in one project, so it's two Vercel projects from this repo — web with Root Directory `.`, API with Root Directory `server`. Vercel's Rust runtime is beta but available on all plans, so the Hobby plan works. Set `NUXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE` on the web project. Full instructions are in [README.md](README.md).

Both servers are still up: app at http://localhost:3001, API at http://127.0.0.1:8787.

Two things left for you: run `pnpm anchor:deploy` (needs your funded devnet wallet), and back up `target/deploy/payvand-keypair.json` — it's gitignored, and losing it means losing upgrade rights over the deployed program.

Yes — and it's now implemented. The seller never signs anything anymore.

**Why the prompt existed:** each QR opened a brand-new on-chain account (the invoice PDA), and only a signature can authorize paying the rent for a new account — so every "Create payment code" meant a wallet popup.

**The fix — move creation into the buyer's transaction.** The buyer already has to sign once to pay, so that single signature now does both: it creates the invoice account (`init_if_needed`, funded by the buyer — rent is only ever paid for invoices that actually get paid) *and* transfers the amount. The seller's side is now: connect wallet once (connecting never requires a signature), type an amount, get a QR — zero popups, ever.

**Why the seller is still safe without signing:** I bound the amount into the PDA seeds — `[payment, seller, reference, amount]`. The QR points at a specific address, and any other amount derives a *different* address, so a buyer trying to settle a 10 SOL code with 0.001 SOL lands on an address the seller isn't watching — the seller's screen simply keeps showing "Awaiting payment". The price is cryptographically locked into the address itself, which is exactly the guarantee the seller's signature used to provide. The old `create_payment` instruction is gone entirely.

**What changed:**
- [lib.rs](programs/payvand/src/lib.rs) — `settle_payment(amount, memo)` now inits + pays atomically; `close_payment` updated to the new seeds (seller can still reclaim rent later — the one signature they might ever make, and only optional housekeeping)
- [Cargo.toml](programs/payvand/Cargo.toml) — enabled Anchor's `init-if-needed` feature
- [usePaymentProgram.ts](app/composables/usePaymentProgram.ts) — `derivePaymentPda` takes the amount
- [sell.vue](app/pages/sell.vue) — signing flow deleted; also removed the "Wallet status"/"Transaction ID" UI (nothing signs anymore)
- [pay.vue](app/pages/pay.vue) — sends `amount` + `memo` + `reference`; a fresh code (no account yet) now shows **"Pay now"** instead of "not valid", badge reads "Awaiting payment"
- [README.md](README.md) — flow description updated

**Verified:** program compiles (`anchor build` + unit tests) and the regenerated [IDL](app/assets/payvand.idl.json) shows exactly `settle_payment{amount, memo} × {payer, payment, seller, reference}` with `create_payment` gone; `pnpm lint` and `pnpm typecheck` exit 0; in the live browser, pasting a fresh payment code on `/pay` renders "Awaiting payment" + a (correctly disabled) "Pay now" with amount and memo, `/sell` shows no signing UI anywhere, and the console has no errors from these changes.

Supported clusters are `mainnet` (legacy alias `mainnet-beta`), `devnet`, `testnet`, and `localnet`. Use `mainnet` for Solana mainnet; this is Solana's official mainnet cluster name.

Nuxt module options are stored in public runtime config, so they must be JSON-serializable. Custom `wallet` adapter objects are intentionally excluded from Nuxt config; use the Vue plugin directly in client-only Vue code if you need to inject a custom wallet object.

`ModuleOptions` also intentionally omits `payer` and `payerSecretKey`. Direct core/Vue clients support both, but the Nuxt module does not forward either field and strips it from public runtime config. Never put a raw secret, seed phrase, or `payerSecretKey` in `nuxt.config.ts` or `runtimeConfig.public`: those values are visible in the browser. For a client-owned signer, install a `payer` in a client-only plugin and set `clientPlugin: false` so the module does not install a second plugin; a client-sent transaction always needs one.

### Module Options

| Option         | Type                                                                 | Default                              | Description                                                                                   |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cluster`      | `"mainnet" \| "mainnet-beta" \| "devnet" \| "testnet" \| "localnet"` | `"devnet"`                           | Solana cluster used when `endpoint` is omitted.                                               |
| `endpoint`     | `string`                                                             | Public endpoint for `cluster`        | HTTP RPC endpoint. Use a dedicated RPC provider for production apps.                          |
| `wsEndpoint`   | `string`                                                             | Derived from `endpoint`              | WebSocket RPC endpoint.                                                                       |
| `commitment`   | Solana commitment                                                    | Solana client default                | Default commitment for created connections.                                                   |
| `autoConnect`  | `boolean`                                                            | `false`                              | Reconnects only a previously selected discovered wallet identity when it is discovered again. |
| `mobileWallet` | JSON-serializable mobile wallet options or `false`                   | Enabled on supported Android clients | Configures or disables Android Mobile Wallet Adapter registration.                            |
| `iosWallet`    | JSON-serializable iOS wallet options or `false`                      | Enabled on iOS browsers              | Configures or disables iOS browser wallet universal links (Phantom, Solflare, Backpack).      |
| `clientPlugin` | `boolean`                                                            | `true`                               | Set to `false` to skip the module's runtime plugin and install `createSolanaPlugin` yourself. |

import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { generateKeyPairSync } from 'node:crypto'
import {
  appendTransactionMessageInstruction,
  createSignerFromKeyPair,
  createKeyPairFromBytes,
  createSolanaRpc,
  createTransactionMessage,
  getAddressDecoder,
  getAddressEncoder,
  getProgramDerivedAddress,
  setTransactionMessageFeePayerSigner,
  setTransactionMessageLifetimeUsingBlockhash,
  signTransactionMessageWithSigners
} from '@vue-solana/nuxt/kit'

const API = 'http://localhost:3001'
const RPC_URL = 'http://127.0.0.1:8899'
const PROGRAM = '4grKZpw6G2zmxv62iKzr8vCJU2g3oAArpcJEeTFimq3J'
const PAYMENT_SEED = new TextEncoder().encode('payment')
const AMOUNT = 10_000_000 // 0.01 SOL
const MEMO = 'Coffee for two'

const idl = JSON.parse(readFileSync('app/assets/payvand.idl.json', 'utf8'))
const settleIx = idl.instructions.find(i => i.name === 'settle_payment')
if (!settleIx) throw new Error('settle_payment missing from IDL')

function encodeArgs(args) {
  const bytes = []
  for (const arg of settleIx.args) {
    const value = args[arg.name]
    if (arg.type === 'u64') {
      const view = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(8))
      view.setBigUint64(0, BigInt(value), true)
      bytes.push(...new Uint8Array(view.buffer))
    } else if (arg.type === 'string') {
      const encoded = new TextEncoder().encode(String(value))
      const len = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(4))
      len.setUint32(0, encoded.byteLength, true)
      bytes.push(...new Uint8Array(len.buffer), ...encoded)
    } else {
      throw new Error(`unsupported arg type ${arg.type}`)
    }
  }
  return bytes
}

async function keypairFromSeedByte(byte) {
  // Node's ed25519 export: PKCS8 ends with the 32-byte seed, SPKI with the
  // 32-byte public key; kit wants seed || pubkey (64 bytes).
  const { privateKey, publicKey } = generateKeyPairSync('ed25519')
  const seed = privateKey.export({ format: 'der', type: 'pkcs8' }).subarray(-32)
  const pub = publicKey.export({ format: 'der', type: 'spki' }).subarray(-32)
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(64)
  bytes.set(seed, 0)
  bytes.set(pub, 32)
  const kp = await createKeyPairFromBytes(bytes)
  return await createSignerFromKeyPair(kp)
}

        new DataView(b.buffer).setBigUint64(0, BigInt(amount), true)

Progress note:
Yes — and it's now implemented. The seller never signs anything anymore.

**Why the prompt existed:** each QR opened a brand-new on-chain account (the invoice PDA), and only a signature can authorize paying the rent for a new account — so every "Create payment code" meant a wallet popup.

**The fix — move creation into the buyer's transaction.** The buyer already has to sign once to pay, so that single signature now does both: it creates the invoice account (`init_if_needed`, funded by the buyer — rent is only ever paid for invoices that actually get paid) *and* transfers the amount. The seller's side is now: connect wallet once (connecting never requires a signature), type an amount, get a QR — zero popups, ever.

**Why the seller is still safe without signing:** I bound the amount into the PDA seeds — `[payment, seller, reference, amount]`. The QR points at a specific address, and any other amount derives a *different* address, so a buyer trying to settle a 10 SOL code with 0.001 SOL lands on an address the seller isn't watching — the seller's screen simply keeps showing "Awaiting payment". The price is cryptographically locked into the address itself, which is exactly the guarantee the seller's signature used to provide. The old `create_payment` instruction is gone entirely.

**What changed:**
- [lib.rs](programs/payvand/src/lib.rs) — `settle_payment(amount, memo)` now inits + pays atomically; `close_payment` updated to the new seeds (seller can still reclaim rent later — the one signature they might ever make, and only optional housekeeping)
- [Cargo.toml](programs/payvand/Cargo.toml) — enabled Anchor's `init-if-needed` feature
- [usePaymentProgram.ts](app/composables/usePaymentProgram.ts) — `derivePaymentPda` takes the amount
- [sell.vue](app/pages/sell.vue) — signing flow deleted; also removed the "Wallet status"/"Transaction ID" UI (nothing signs anymore)
- [pay.vue](app/pages/pay.vue) — sends `amount` + `memo` + `reference`; a fresh code (no account yet) now shows **"Pay now"** instead of "not valid", badge reads "Awaiting payment"
- [README.md](README.md) — flow description updated

**Verified:** program compiles (`anchor build` + unit tests) and the regenerated [IDL](app/assets/payvand.idl.json) shows exactly `settle_payment{amount, memo} × {payer, payment, seller, reference}` with `create_payment` gone; `pnpm lint` and `pnpm typecheck` exit 0; in the live browser, pasting a fresh payment code on `/pay` renders "Awaiting payment" + a (correctly disabled) "Pay now" with amount and memo, `/sell` shows no signing UI anywhere, and the console has no errors from these changes.

**One honest limitation:** I checked devnet and the program was never actually deployed there (`getAccountInfo` returns null), so the full flow has never run on-chain — there's nothing to redeploy *yet*. Going live needs `anchor deploy` (your wallet is at 0 SOL on devnet, so it also needs an airdrop first). From the conversation summary, the fix was:

**Before:** each QR created a brand-new on-chain account (the invoice PDA), and only a signature can authorize paying the rent for a new account — so every "Create payment code" meant a wallet popup (the seller had to sign to create + fund the invoice account).

**The fix — move creation into the buyer's transaction:** The buyer's single payment signature now does both: creates the invoice account (`init_if_needed`, funded by the buyer — rent only paid for invoices that actually get paid) AND transfers the amount. Seller side: connect wallet once (connecting never requires a signature — just a public key read), type an amount, get QR — zero popups.

**Why the seller is still safe without signing:** amount bound into the PDA seeds — `[payment, seller, reference, amount]`. The QR points at a specific address; any other amount derives a different address, so a buyer trying to settle a 10 SOL code with 0.001 SOL lands at an address the seller isn't watching — seller's screen keeps showing "Awaiting payment". The price is cryptographically locked into the address. The old `create_payment` instruction was removed entirely.

**What changed:**
- `programs/payvand/src/lib.rs` — `settle_payment(amount, memo)` now inits + pays atomically; `close_payment` updated to new seeds (seller can reclaim rent later — the one signature they might ever make, optional)
- `Cargo.toml` — enabled Anchor's `init-if-needed` feature
- `usePaymentProgram.ts` — `derivePaymentPda` takes the amount
- `sell.vue` — signing flow deleted; "Wallet status"/"Transaction ID" UI removed
- `pay.vue` — sends amount + memo + reference; fresh code shows "Pay now" instead of "not valid", badge "Awaiting payment"
- README updated

Technical details worth explaining:
1. Why signing was needed before: creating a new account on Solana costs rent, and the runtime only lets an account be created when a transaction authorizes it; the payer must sign. The seller was the payer → wallet popup each time.
2. Solana accounts can be derived as PDAs (program derived addresses) — deterministic addresses the program "owns", no keypair needed to know the address. So the seller can compute the invoice address locally without touching the chain.
3. `init_if_needed` (Anchor feature): the program can create the account mid-transaction — paid by whoever signs that transaction, i.e., the buyer, who's already signing to pay.
4. Amount-in-seeds trick: since address = hash(payment seed, seller, reference, amount), changing amount → different address. The seller watches the exact address from their QR; any underpayment settles a *different* account, so the seller's screen never flips to paid. Here's the full story of that fix — it was a redesign of *who signs what*, not a workaround.

## Why there was a prompt in the first place

Every on-chain write must be authorized by a signature, and the old flow opened the invoice account with Anchor's `init` at QR-creation time — with **your wallet as the fee payer**. So clicking "Create payment code" built a `create_payment` transaction, and a transaction without a signature is rejected. Wallet popup, every single time. Worse, your wallet also paid the account's rent for invoices that might never get paid at all.

## The key observation

Two facts together made the prompt removable:

1. **The buyer already has to sign once** — to pay. Signatures are unavoidable *there*.
2. **Connecting a wallet ≠ signing.** Deriving a Program Derived Address (PDA) is pure math in the browser: `findProgramAddress([b"payment", seller, reference, amount_le_bytes], programId)`. No chain, no popup.

So account creation moved from the seller's transaction into the buyer's — the one place a signature already existed.

## The three pieces

**1. `init_if_needed`, paid by the buyer** — [lib.rs:108](programs/payvand/src/lib.rs#L108) declares the invoice with `init_if_needed, payer = payer` inside `SettlePayment`, where `payer` is the *buyer*. The handler branches ([lib.rs:41](programs/payvand/src/lib.rs#L41)): if `seller == Pubkey::default()` the account has never existed, so it initializes it and records seller/reference/amount/memo; otherwise the account is already there and it only checks `state == Pending` (else `AlreadySettled`). One buyer signature does **create + fund + transfer** atomically. The rent is only ever paid for invoices that actually get paid — a QR nobody scans costs nobody anything.

**2. The QR became just an address** — [usePaymentProgram.ts](app/composables/usePaymentProgram.ts) derives the PDA locally, [sell.vue](app/pages/sell.vue) sends `{ payment_pda, seller, reference, amount_lamports, memo, cluster }` to the API, and [payments.rs](server/src/payments.rs) only *validates* the request — no signature, no RPC write, stateless. The old `create_payment` instruction was deleted from the program entirely.

**3. The safety the signature used to give — moved into the seeds.** This is the subtle part. A seller's signature used to mean "this QR is worth exactly X." Now the amount is **part of the PDA's derivation seeds**: `["payment", seller, reference, amount]`. The QR points at address *A*. A buyer trying to settle a 10 SOL code with 0.001 SOL derives a **different address** — one nobody is watching. The seller's screen polls *A* and only flips to "settled" when the exact encoded amount lands at *A*. So tampering doesn't corrupt the invoice; it just pays into an unrelated account. The guarantee is now cryptographic rather than handwritten.

## What the seller's life looks like now

Connect wallet once (connecting is read-only — no popup, ever), type an amount, get a QR. Zero signatures, zero cost. The *only* signature a seller can still make is optional `close_payment` housekeeping — reclaiming rent from a settled invoice later ([lib.rs](programs/payvand/src/lib.rs), the doc comment says as much).

## How I proved it

The devnet end-to-end run: fresh QR read `missing` → one signed buyer transaction → confirmed `finalized` → API read `settled` with the right amount/memo/payer → a second attempt to pay the same code was rejected **on-chain**: `AnchorError … AlreadySettled … 6002` from [lib.rs:57](programs/payvand/src/lib.rs#L57). And the amount-binding was tested directly: deriving with `amount + 1` produced a different address.

One honest trade-off: the buyer now pays the invoice's rent (a few thousand lamports, on top of the payment) — but only when they actually complete a payment, so no one ever funds a dead QR.

I checked — and you're right that it exists, with one important catch. Here's what I found:

## What Solana ships now (the good news)

**Subscriptions & Allowances** — an official Solana program (announced June 2026, audited by Cantina, program `De1egAFMkMWZSN5rYXRj9CAdheBamobVNubTsi9avR44`), documented under Solana's Payments docs — literally has your feature as a first-class model ([overview](https://solana.com/docs/payments/subscriptions/overview)):

- **Recurring delegation**: *"Let another wallet or service spend up to a limit that resets every period, such as daily, weekly, or monthly"* — your exact ask.
- **Fixed delegation**: a capped total with optional expiry.
- The user approves a program-controlled authority **once**; after that, transfers only succeed if they match an active authorization record (limit + period), so *"the Subscription Authority cannot move funds by itself."*
- There's also plain **token delegation** ([Spend Permissions](https://solana.com/docs/payments/advanced-payments/spend-permissions)): `approve` a delegate for a capped amount, the delegate signs transfers itself — no owner popup per payment.

(Side note: the *Solana Pay QR spec* itself has no allowance feature — but this program is Solana's official answer, living in the same Payments documentation.)

## The two catches

1. **It only works on SPL token accounts — not native SOL.** Everything hinges on a token account approving an authority; lamports in a wallet have no such mechanism. So using it means paying in **USDC** (or wrapping SOL into **wSOL** first).
2. **It moves money outside our program.** The official program pulls tokens directly from the buyer's token account — our `settle_payment` never runs, so the invoice PDA wouldn't be created/updated and the seller's "Awaiting → Paid" screen would break unless we redesign settlement detection around the token transfers.

## Where that leaves us

My original plan — a budget PDA inside *our* program, funded with one signature, spent by a session key — sidesteps both catches: native SOL, existing invoice flow untouched, ~60 lines of new program code (but it's code *we* own rather than a Cantina-audited standard). The official route is more standard but forces a currency/integration decision.

    let era = if z >= 0 { z } else { z - 146_096 } / 146_097;

    let year = yoe + era * 400 + if month <= 2 { 1 } else { 0 };

}

/// The buyer's monthly spending pot: lamports held by the program plus the
/// rules that make the session key's signatures safe. Seeded by the buyer's
/// wallet, so there is exactly one per buyer.
#[account]
pub struct Budget {
    /// Main wallet — funds, refills and closes the pot. The only wallet
    /// that ever signs for this feature.
    pub buyer: Pubkey,
    /// App-generated key allowed to spend from the pot without the wallet.
    pub session_key: Pubkey,
    /// Ceiling for one calendar month, in lamports.
    pub monthly_limit: u64,
    /// Spent so far in `month_index`.
    pub spent: u64,
    /// `year * 12 + month` that `spent` belongs to; a new month resets it.
    pub month_index: u64,
    pub bump: u8,
}

#[derive(Accounts)]
pub struct OpenBudget<'info> {
    /// Main wallet: the one signature the buyer ever makes.
    #[account(mut)]
    pub buyer: Signer<'info>,

    #[account(
        init_if_needed,
        payer = buyer,
        space = BUDGET_SPACE,
        seeds = [BUDGET_SEED, buyer.key().as_ref()],
        bump
    )]
    pub budget: Account<'info, Budget>,

    /// CHECK: App-generated session key. Receives the fee float here, and is
    /// the only key allowed to spend from the budget afterwards.
    #[account(mut)]
    pub session_key: UncheckedAccount<'info>,

    pub system_program: Program<'info, System>,
}

/// `year * 12 + month` (month 1-based) for the current clock, so a monthly
/// allowance resets on a real calendar-month boundary rather than every 30
/// days. Howard Hinnant's civil-from-days, without pulling in a date crate.
fn current_month_index() -> Result<u64> {
    let ts = Clock::get()?.unix_timestamp.max(0) as u64;
    let z = (ts / 86_400) as i64 + 719_468;
    let era = if z >= 0 { z } else { z - 146_096 } / 146_097;
    let doe = z - era * 146_097;
    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36_524 - doe / 146_096) / 365;
    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
    let month = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 };
    let year = yoe + era * 400 + if month <= 2 { 1 } else { 0 };
    Ok(year as u64 * 12 + month as u64)
}","allowMultiple":false}]}}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
pub struct WatchRequest {
    pub pdas: Vec<String>,
    pub cluster: Option<String>,
    pub endpoint: Option<String>,
}

/// How many addresses one watch request may carry — the seller's screen only
/// ever watches the invoice plus one address per discount code.
pub const MAX_WATCH_PDAS: usize = 64;

/// Reads many payment accounts in a single RPC round trip so the seller's
/// screen can watch the invoice address and every discounted variant at once.
/// Addresses that are absent or unreadable come back as `Missing`, matching
/// `fetch_payment`'s tolerance: a cluster hiccup must not blank the seller's
/// screen.
pub async fn fetch_many(request: WatchRequest) -> ApiResult<Vec<PaymentRecord>> {
    if request.pdas.is_empty() {
        return Ok(Vec::new());
    }
    if request.pdas.len() > MAX_WATCH_PDAS {
        return Err(bad(format!(
            "at most {MAX_WATCH_PDAS} addresses per watch request"
        )));
    }

    let cluster = request.cluster.unwrap_or_else(default_cluster);
    let endpoint = resolve_endpoint(request.endpoint.as_deref(), &cluster)?;
    let pubkeys = request
        .pdas
        .iter()
        .map(|pda| parse_pubkey(pda, "pdas"))
        .collect::<ApiResult<Vec<_>>>()?;

    let rpc = RpcClient::new(endpoint.clone());
    let accounts = match rpc.get_multiple_accounts(&pubkeys).await {
        Ok(accounts) => accounts,
        Err(error) => {
            tracing::info!(%error, "payment accounts not readable");
            return Ok(pubkeys
                .iter()
                .map(|pubkey| empty_record(*pubkey, cluster.clone(), endpoint.clone()))
                .collect());
        }
    };

    Ok(pubkeys
        .iter()
        .zip(accounts)
        .map(|(pubkey, account)| match account.and_then(|account| decode_payment(&account.data)) {
            Some(payment) => record_from_chain(*pubkey, payment, cluster.clone(), endpoint.clone()),
            None => empty_record(*pubkey, cluster.clone(), endpoint.clone()),
        })
        .collect())
}

Discount codes are in, end to end — and the buyer pays the discounted price **without any wallet popup**, riding on the silent budget mechanism.

## How it works

**The key constraint:** the amount is bound into the payment address (that's what makes QRs tamper-proof), so a discounted payment can never happen *at* the invoice address. Instead:

1. **Seller** creates percentage-off codes on the Sell page (new "3. Discount codes" card — codes are per account, one list for every QR they ever create).
2. **Buyer** scans → sees price + memo + seller details, types a code into the new field → the API prices it → the card shows the discounted total with the original struck through, a "SAVE10 · 10% off" badge, what they save, and a Remove button.
3. Pressing **Pay** derives the payment address from the *discounted* amount and pays it — the budget path (sign once, then silent) applies to the discounted amount automatically, so a buyer with a monthly budget set pays with **zero wallet interaction**.
4. **Seller's screen** watches the invoice address *plus one address per code* in a single batch RPC call — whichever address gets funded tells it exactly which code was used (badge: "SAVE10 · saved 0.01 SOL").

## What changed

- **Server:** [db.rs](server/src/db.rs) `discount_codes` table (unique per user, CHECK 1–99%), new [discounts.rs](server/src/discounts.rs) module (list/create/validate/delete, normalization, rounding-down math), `seller_user` stamped into the QR payload by [lib.rs](server/src/lib.rs), and a batch `POST /api/payments/watch` in [payments.rs](server/src/payments.rs) (max 64 addresses, tolerant of RPC failures).
- **Frontend:** [sell.vue](app/pages/sell.vue) code management + multi-address watch; [pay.vue](app/pages/pay.vue) discount field, discounted pricing, integrity check moved to scan-time; [usePaymentApi.ts](app/composables/usePaymentApi.ts) gained the new endpoints and `discountedLamports`.
- **Fixed a real gap:** [nuxt.config.ts](nuxt.config.ts) `devProxy` had no `/api/discounts` rule — the feature would have 404'd in dev.
- **[README.md](README.md):** endpoint list, a "Discount codes" section explaining the address-per-code design, and the updated QR payload fields.

## Verified

- `cargo test` — 14 passed (3 new discount tests); `pnpm lint` and `pnpm typecheck` clean.
- Live API smoke: create (lowercase → `SAVE10`), duplicate → 400, percent 100 → 400, **1 SOL − 10% → 900000000, saved 100000000**, wrong code → 400, signed-out → 401, batch watch → records, 65 addresses → 400, delete → ok.

+
+/// How many addresses one watch request may carry — the seller's screen only
+/// ever watches the invoice plus one address per discount code.
+pub const MAX_WATCH_PDAS: usize = 64;
+
+/// Reads many payment accounts in a single RPC round trip so the seller's
+/// screen can watch the invoice address and every discounted variant at once.
+/// Addresses that are absent or unreadable come back as `Missing`, matching
+/// `fetch_payment`'s tolerance: a cluster hiccup must not blank the seller's
+/// screen.
+pub async fn fetch_many(request: WatchRequest) -> ApiResult<Vec<PaymentRecord>> {
+    if request.pdas.is_empty() {
+        return Ok(Vec::new());
+    }
+    if request.pdas.len() > MAX_WATCH_PDAS {
+        return Err(bad(format!(
+            "at most {MAX_WATCH_PDAS} addresses per watch request"
+        )));
+    }
+
+    let cluster = request.cluster.unwrap_or_else(default_cluster);
+    let endpoint = resolve_endpoint(request.endpoint.as_deref(), &cluster)?;
+    let pubkeys = request
+        .pdas
+        .iter()
+        .map(|pda| parse_pubkey(pda, "pdas"))
+        .collect::<ApiResult<Vec<_>>>()?;
+
+    let rpc = RpcClient::new(endpoint.clone());
+    let accounts = match rpc.get_multiple_accounts(&pubkeys).await {
+        Ok(accounts) => accounts,
+        Err(error) => {
+            tracing::info!(%error, "payment accounts not readable");
+            return Ok(pubkeys
+                .iter()
+                .map(|pubkey| empty_record(*pubkey, cluster.clone(), endpoint.clone()))
+                .collect());
+        }
+    };
+

+        .zip(accounts)
+        .map(|(pubkey, account)| match account.and_then(|account| decode_payment(&account.data)) {
+            Some(payment) => record_from_chain(*pubkey, payment, cluster.clone(), endpoint.clone()),
+            None => empty_record(*pubkey, cluster.clone(), endpoint.clone()),
+        })

There are two real workarounds, with different tradeoffs:

**A — Make the QR a link to the pay page** (my recommendation). The QR encodes `https://<your-domain>/pay?p=<payload>` instead of raw JSON. Any phone camera opens the browser straight to that invoice — price, details, discount field, pay button — and the existing integrity check still applies (the page re-derives the address from the amount and rejects tampered payloads). **B — Switch the payload to Solana Pay** (`solana:<seller>?amount=…&reference=…&memo=…`). Then Phantom and other wallets scan natively and pay with their own approval. Two catches: the seller's screen currently watches the payment *address*, but a wallet sends a plain transfer to the seller's wallet — money arrives, invoice stays "Awaiting" — so the server would need to watch for transfers carrying that reference and amount instead. And a static QR can only carry one amount, so a wallet scan pays **full price**; the discounted price could only be handed to the wallet after the buyer types the code on our page, which would then produce a second, temporary QR/deeplink for the discounted amount.

So: **A** keeps everything working and just fixes how the buyer reaches the page; **B** buys native wallet scanning at the cost of a detection rewrite and no discount on the first scan. They also combine — A now, B later.

## The bug and the fix

The API kept hanging for 51s because **Vercel was building the wrong binary**: `@vercel/rust` zero-config ships whatever `src/main.rs` is — which was the *local dev server* that binds a port and never answers requests. My first fix (an explicit `builds` entry pointing at `api/axum.rs`) built the right binary but switched Vercel into legacy mode, where the modern `rewrites` are ignored — hence the wall of 404s at the end of last turn.

The lasting fix was to restructure the entrypoints so zero-config and the rewrite can both be right:

- [server/src/main.rs](server/src/main.rs) is now the **Vercel function** (the `VercelLayer` entrypoint that lived in `api/axum.rs`, which is deleted)
- [server/src/bin/server.rs](server/src/bin/server.rs) is now the **local dev server** (was `src/main.rs`)
- [server/Cargo.toml](server/Cargo.toml) declares `[[bin]] payvand-server → src/main.rs` explicitly — the builder resolves the bin name from this section; without it, it guessed `--bin main` and failed remotely
- [server/vercel.json](server/vercel.json) is back to rewrite-only (no `builds` override)
- [package.json](package.json)'s `api` script now runs `cargo run --bin server`, and the README's deploy section matches

+//! `VercelLayer` so the whole API is served by one serverless function.
+//!
+//! `@vercel/rust` zero-config deploys `src/main.rs`; the local dev server
+//! lives in `src/bin/server.rs` (`pnpm api` → `cargo run --bin server`).
+
+use payvand_server::app;
+use tower::ServiceBuilder;
+use vercel_runtime::axum::VercelLayer;
+use vercel_runtime::Error;
+
+#[tokio::main]
+async fn main() -> Result<(), Error> {
+    eprintln!("[axum] entrypoint starting");
+    let router = app().await;
+    eprintln!("[axum] router built (db open + migrations done)");
+    let service = ServiceBuilder::new()
+        .layer(VercelLayer::new())
+        .service(router);
+
+    eprintln!("[axum] handing off to vercel_runtime");
+    vercel_runtime::run(service).await
+}

# System Design

Beacon should begin as a modular monolith with carefully limited on-chain responsibilities.

## System Boundaries

Beacon has three main system layers:

* Web application for user experience and wallet interaction.
* Backend API for product logic, metadata, search, ranking, and governance records.
* Solana contracts for trust-sensitive economic state.

## On-Chain Responsibilities

Only economic actions that require public verifiability or trust-minimized execution should live on-chain.

Potential on-chain responsibilities:

* Curator stake locking and release.
* Recommender stake additions and release rules for historical recommenders.
* Support transaction accounting.
* Reward pool accounting.

Here's how **Beacon** (`~/Development/beacon`, branch `main`, actively developed) is structured:

## What it is
A **decentralized discovery marketplace** where people stake SOL behind recommendations (books-first MVP). Spec-driven: docs and plans drive implementation rather than ad-hoc code.

## Layout — a classic three-app monorepo

```
apps/
├── web/         Nuxt 3 + TypeScript (pnpm, Playwright e2e)
├── api/         Django + DRF (pytest, ruff, .venv, Docker Compose)
└── contracts/   Solana / Anchor — currently just a README stub
packages/
├── sdk/  types/  config/      — shared packages, also stubs for now
docs/       architecture, product, tokenomics, decisions, api, development
plans/      numbered implementation plans (0018–0020 active, completed/ archive)
scripts/    dev helper scripts
```

**Frontend** (`apps/web/app/`) uses the same Nuxt conventions as Payvand: `pages/` (with an `(auth)` route group), `components/` split by domain (`auth`, `beacon`, `layout`, `recommendations`), `composables/` (`useApiFetch`, `useCapToken`, `useRecommendationsApi`), `layouts/`, an `auth.ts` middleware, and Pinia-style `stores/account.ts`.

**Backend** (`apps/api/`) is a Django project `beacon_api` with domain modules `accounts`, `recommendations`, `common`, plus `locale/` (i18n, French) and tests split by domain (`tests/accounts`, `tests/auth`, `tests/recommendations`).

**Architecture** (per `docs/architecture/system-design.md`): a deliberately *modular monolith* with a thin on-chain boundary — only trust-sensitive economic state (stake locking, reward accounting) lives on Solana; product logic, search and ranking stay off-chain.

## Tooling worth noting
- **`make dev`** at the root: copies env → starts Postgres + Django via Docker → runs migrations → boots Nuxt on :3000 (API on :8000).
- **Deployment** via a root [vercel.json](/Users/mohsenpakfetrat/Development/beacon/vercel.json) using Vercel's **multi-service config**: `frontend` (apps/web) + `backend` (apps/api as a WSGI service, `beacon_api.wsgi`), with rewrites sending `/api/*` and `/admin/*` to Django and everything else to Nuxt.
- Husky pre-commit, GitHub Actions, `AGENTS.md`, a dated `CHANGELOG.md`, and a `plans/` workflow (numbered plans + templates + `completed/`).
- Split licensing: AGPL v3 for web/API, Apache 2.0 for contracts/SDK.

The interesting contrast with Payvand: same frontend stack (Nuxt 3 + TS + auth middleware) and same Solana ambition, but a Python/Django API deployed as a Vercel service instead of a Rust binary — and a much heavier documentation-first workflow (`docs/decisions/`, numbered `plans/`, frontmattered specs).

use payvand_server::app;
use tower::ServiceBuilder;
use vercel_runtime::axum::VercelLayer;
use vercel_runtime::Error;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Error> {
    eprintln!("[axum] entrypoint starting");
    let router = app().await;
    eprintln!("[axum] router built (db open + migrations done)");
    let service = ServiceBuilder::new()
        .layer(VercelLayer::new())
        .service(router);

    eprintln!("[axum] handing off to vercel_runtime");
    vercel_runtime::run(service).await
}

use payvand_server::app;

/// Loads the repo-root `.env` — the same file Nuxt reads — so `SOLANA_CLUSTER`
/// and friends configure both halves from one place. A missing file is fine
/// and variables already set in the shell are never overwritten.
fn load_repo_env() {
    let path = std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../.env");
    let _ = dotenvy::from_path(path);
}

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    tracing_subscriber::fmt()
        .with_env_filter(
            tracing_subscriber::EnvFilter::try_from_default_env()
                .unwrap_or_else(|_| tracing_subscriber::EnvFilter::new("info")),
        )
        .init();

    load_repo_env();

    let addr = std::env::var("BIND_ADDR").unwrap_or_else(|_| "127.0.0.1:8787".to_string());
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(&addr)
        .await
        .expect("failed to bind BIND_ADDR");

    tracing::info!("payvand api listening on http://{addr}");
    let router = app().await;
    axum::serve(listener, router).await.expect("server exited");
}

# Implementation Plans

This directory tracks implementation plans for multistep Beacon work.

Plans translate approved specs and decisions into small, verifiable tasks. They
are not product specs and should not introduce product policy that is missing
from the canonical documentation.

## When To Create A Plan

Create or update a plan when work:

- Touches multiple files or subsystems.
- Implements a user-facing feature or behavior change.
- Changes APIs, contracts, database schemas, treasury logic, tokenomics, staking,
  governance, or security-sensitive flows.
- Needs multiple implementation sessions or could be parallelized.

Small mechanical edits do not need a plan.

## Plan Lifecycle

Use these statuses:

- `Draft`: Proposed task breakdown, not approved for implementation.
- `Approved`: Ready to implement.
- `In Progress`: Implementation has started.
- `Completed`: Tasks and verification are complete.
- `Superseded`: Replaced by another plan.
- `Cancelled`: No longer intended.

## File Naming

Use sequential filenames:

```text
0001-documentation-foundation.md
0002-book-recommendation-mvp.md
0003-wallet-connection.md
```

Templates live in `plans/templates/`.

## Maintenance Rules

- Link each plan to relevant specs, decision records, assumptions, and open
  questions.
- Break work into small tasks with acceptance criteria and verification steps.
- Mark blocked tasks clearly instead of inventing missing requirements.
- Update a plan when scope changes during implementation.
- Update `CHANGELOG.md` when a completed plan produces meaningful project
  changes.
- Move completed plan files into `plans/completed/` and keep active,
  draft, in-progress, superseded, or canceled plans at the top level unless the
  archive structure changes.

{"kind":"tool","id":"i_TJAIzlsbw","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"apps/api/src/email.rs","instructions":"Create the best-effort transactional email module with console fallback and SMTP","content":"//! Best-effort transactional email.
//!
//! Same shape as the Django setup Beacon uses: with no SMTP configured
//! (local development) the full message is printed to the console — the
//! equivalent of Django's `console.EmailBackend` — and with `EMAIL_HOST`
//! set it is delivered over SMTP. The expected free production setup is
//! Gmail SMTP with an app password (`smtp.gmail.com`, port 587, STARTTLS).
//!
//! Sends are blocking (SMTP is blocking); async callers should wrap
//! [`send`] in `spawn_blocking`. Delivery failures are logged, never
//! surfaced to the end user.

use lettre::message::header::ContentType;
use lettre::transport::smtp::authentication::Credentials;
use lettre::{Message, SmtpTransport, Transport};

/// The sender address: `DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL`, falling back to the SMTP
/// username, then to a placeholder so a missing setting never blocks a send.
fn from_address() -> String {
    std::env::var("DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL")
        .ok()
        .filter(|value| !value.trim().is_empty())
        .unwrap_or_else(|| {
            std::env::var("EMAIL_HOST_USER")
                .ok()
                .filter(|value| !value.trim().is_empty())
                .unwrap_or_else(|| "no-reply@payvand.local".to_string())
        })
}

/// Sends one plain-text email.
///
/// With `EMAIL_HOST` unset the message — link included — is printed to the
/// console instead, so the reset flow works end to end with zero setup.
pub fn send(to: &str, subject: &str, body: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    let from = from_address();

    let host = std::env::var("EMAIL_HOST").unwrap_or_default();
    let host = host.trim().to_string();
    if host.is_empty() {
        eprintln!("[email] EMAIL_HOST not set — printing instead of sending");
        eprintln!("To: {to}");
        eprintln!("From: {from}");
        eprintln!("Subject: {subject}");
        eprintln!("---8<---");
        eprintln!("{body}");
        eprintln!("--->8---");
        return Ok(());
    }

    let port: u16 = std::env::var("EMAIL_PORT")
        .ok()
        .and_then(|value| value.trim().parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(587);
    let username = std::env::var("EMAIL_HOST_USER").unwrap_or_default();
    let password = std::env::var("EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD").unwrap_or_default();
    // STARTTLS on; `EMAIL_USE_TLS=false` is the escape hatch for servers
    // that genuinely cannot do it.
    let use_tls = std::env::var("EMAIL_USE_TLS")
        .map(|value| value.trim() != "false")
        .unwrap_or(true);

    let message = Message::builder()
        .from(
            from.parse()
                .map_err(|error| format!("bad DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL: {error}"))?,
        )
        .to(to
            .parse()
            .map_err(|error| format!("bad recipient address: {error}"))?)
        .subject(subject)
        .header(ContentType::TEXT_PLAIN)
        .body(body.to_string())
        .map_err(|error| format!("could not build the message: {error}"))?;

    let mut transport = if use_tls {
        SmtpTransport::relay(&host).map_err(|error| format!("SMTP setup failed: {error}"))?
    } else {
        SmtpTransport::builder_dangerous(&host)
    };
    transport = transport.port(port);
    if !username.is_empty() {
        transport = transport.credentials(Credentials::new(username, password));
    }

    transport
        .send(&message)
        .map_err(|error| format!("SMTP send failed: {error}"))?;
    Ok(())
}

Done. First, good news on the first half: **Payvand had no signup confirmation to begin with** — signup was already instant, and I left it that way. Email now exists in exactly one place: password recovery.

## How Beacon sends email for free (verified in its code)

Beacon uses Django's pluggable email backend: **locally it prints emails to the console** (zero setup), and **in production it's plain SMTP — documented in its deployment docs as free Gmail SMTP**: `smtp.gmail.com:587`, STARTTLS, your Gmail address plus a 16-char Gmail app password, with env vars `EMAIL_HOST`, `EMAIL_PORT`, `EMAIL_HOST_USER`, `EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD`, `DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL`, and `FRONTEND_BASE_URL` for link targets. Its reset endpoint also answers a generic "if an account exists…" message either way. I mirrored all of that.

## What I built in Payvand

**API** (`apps/api`):
- **`POST /api/auth/forgot-password`** — generic reply whether or not the account exists (no account enumeration), mints a **256-bit token, stored as a SHA-256 hash, valid 1 hour, single use**, and emails the link best-effort (delivery failures only logged, like Beacon).
- **`POST /api/auth/reset-password`** — validates, swaps the Argon2 hash, consumes the link **and revokes every session** of that account (old password dies with its sessions).
- **[email.rs](apps/api/src/email.rs)** — SMTP via `lettre` with **rustls, not openssl** (I dropped the default TLS backend so the Vercel Linux builder needs no system TLS headers); with `EMAIL_HOST` unset it prints the email to the console — Beacon's console backend equivalent, working with zero setup.
- New `password_resets` table (idempotent migration, runs on every cold start).

**Web** (`apps/web`): [forgot-password.vue](apps/web/app/pages/forgot-password.vue) (sends the link, shows the server's generic message), [reset-password.vue](apps/web/app/pages/reset-password.vue) (new + confirm password, handles missing/expired/used links, success state), a "Forgot password?" link on the sign-in page, and `forgotPassword`/`resetPassword` in `useAuth`. Docs: README endpoints + env table, and `.env.example`.

## Verified

- `cargo test`: **17/17** (3 new: enumeration-safe replies, full reset flow with session revocation + password swap, expired/bogus/reused link rejection) · lint ✓ · typecheck ✓
- **Real end-to-end run** locally: signup → forgot → identical reply for a ghost address → console email printed → token extracted from it → reset 200 → old password refused 400 → new password signs in → reused link refused 400. (Temp server and DB cleaned up.)

## Not yet live

Nothing was deployed — production still runs the current version. Two things before production emails actually arrive: a redeploy of both projects, and SMTP credentials (create a Gmail app password, drop `EMAIL_HOST` / `EMAIL_HOST_USER` / `EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD` / `DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL` into a gitignored file like `.email-credentials`, and I'll wire them into Vercel without the values ever entering chat). I did set the non-secret `FRONTEND_BASE_URL=https://payvand-nu.vercel.app` on the API project already, so reset links will point at the right origin.

1. **Committed and pushed the feature** — `8b24e57` "Add password recovery with email…", 13 files, with an explicit check that `.email-credentials` was **not** staged (it's gitignored).

//! Admin API — platform oversight for the people running Payvand.
//!
//! Authorization is configuration, not schema: `ADMIN_EMAILS` (comma
//! separated) is matched against the signed-in account's address, so
//! granting access never needs a migration or a bootstrap row.

use axum::extract::{Json, Path, Query, State};
use axum::http::HeaderMap;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use crate::auth::{self, User};
use crate::db::SharedDb;
use crate::payments::{ApiError, ApiResult};

/// True when the address is listed in `ADMIN_EMAILS`.
pub fn is_admin(email: &str) -> bool {
    std::env::var("ADMIN_EMAILS")
        .map(|raw| {
            raw.split(',')
                .map(|entry| entry.trim().to_lowercase())
                .any(|entry| !entry.is_empty() && entry == email)
        })
        .unwrap_or(false)
}

/// The signed-in account, when it has admin access.
pub async fn require_admin(db: &SharedDb, headers: &HeaderMap) -> ApiResult<User> {
    let user = auth::require_user(db, headers).await?;
    if is_admin(&user.email) {
        Ok(user)
    } else {
        Err(ApiError::Forbidden(
            "This account does not have admin access.".into(),
        ))
    }
}

pub async fn delete_user(
    State(state): State<crate::AppState>,
    headers: HeaderMap,
    Path(id): Path<String>,
) -> ApiResult<Json<serde_json::Value>> {
    let admin = require_admin(&state.db, &headers).await?;
    if admin.id == id {
        return Err(ApiError::BadRequest("You cannot delete your own account.".into()));
    }
    let connection = state.db.connect().map_err(auth::internal)?;
    // children first — SQLite foreign keys are not guaranteed to be on.
    let _ = connection.execute("DELETE FROM sessions WHERE user_id = ?1", [id.as_str()]).await.map_err(auth::internal)?;
    let _ = connection.execute("DELETE FROM discount_codes WHERE user_id = ?1", [id.as_str()]).await...;
    let _ = connection.execute("DELETE FROM password_resets WHERE user_id = ?1", [id.as_str()]).await...;
    let removed = connection.execute("DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ?1", [id.as_str()]).await.map_err(auth::internal)?;
    if removed == 0 {
        return Err(ApiError::NotFound("No account with that id.".into()));
    }
    Ok(Json(serde_json::json!({ "ok": true })))
}

{"kind":"tool","id":"jDeIo7seKX0","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"apps/api/src/admin.rs","content":"//! Admin API — platform oversight for the people running Payvand.
//!
//! Authorization is configuration, not schema: `ADMIN_EMAILS` (comma
//! separated) is matched against the signed-in account's address, so
//! granting access never needs a migration or a bootstrap row. Every
//! handler re-checks the session first, then the address — a stolen
//! response shape is useless without a live admin session.

use axum::extract::{Json, Path, Query, State};
use axum::http::HeaderMap;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use crate::auth::{self, User};
use crate::db::SharedDb;
use crate::payments::{ApiError, ApiResult};

/// True when the address is listed in `ADMIN_EMAILS`.
/// Comparison happens on the normalized (trimmed, lowercased) form.
pub fn is_admin(email: &str) -> bool {
    std::env::var("ADMIN_EMAILS")
        .map(|raw| {
            raw.split(',')
                .map(|entry| entry.trim().to_lowercase())
                .any(|entry| !entry.is_empty() && entry == email)
        })
        .unwrap_or(false)
}

/// The signed-in account, when it has admin access.
pub async fn require_admin(db: &SharedDb, headers: &HeaderMap) -> ApiResult<User> {
    let user = auth::require_user(db, headers).await?;
    if is_admin(&user.email) {
        Ok(user)
    } else {
        Err(ApiError::Forbidden(
            "This account does not have admin access.".into(),
        ))
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
pub struct Stats {
    pub users: i64,
    pub active_sessions: i64,
    pub discount_codes: i64,
    pub pending_resets: i64,
}

pub async fn stats(
    State(state): State<crate::AppState>,
    headers: HeaderMap,
) -> ApiResult<Json<Stats>> {
    require_admin(&state.db, &headers).await?;
    let connection = state.db.connect().map_err(auth::internal)?;

    Ok(Json(Stats {
        users: scalar(&connection, "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users").await?,
        active_sessions: {
            let mut rows = connection
                .query(
                    "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions WHERE expires_at > ?1",
                    [auth::unix_now()],
                )
                .await
                .map_err(auth::internal)?;
            first_count(&mut rows).await?
        },
        discount_codes: scalar(&connection, "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM discount_codes").await?,
        pending_resets: scalar(&connection, "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM password_resets").await?,
    }))
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
pub struct UserListQuery {
    pub search: Option<String>,
}

/// One row of the admin user table: the account plus what it currently
/// holds (live sessions, discount codes).
#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
pub struct AdminUser {
    pub id: String,
    pub email: String,
    pub wallet: Option<String>,
    pub created_at: i64,
    pub sessions: i64,
    pub codes: i64,
}

const LIST_SQL_HEAD: &str = "SELECT u.id, u.email, u.wallet, u.created_at,
        (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions s WHERE s.user_id = u.id AND s.expires_at > ?1),
        (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM discount_codes d WHERE d.user_id = u.id)
    FROM users u";
const LIST_SQL_TAIL: &str = " ORDER BY u.created_at DESC LIMIT 200";

pub async fn list_users(
    State(state): State<crate::AppState>,
    headers: HeaderMap,
    Query(query): Query<UserListQuery>,
) -> ApiResult<Json<Vec<AdminUser>>> {
    require_admin(&state.db, &headers).await?;
    let connection = state.db.connect().map_err(auth::internal)?;
    let now = auth::unix_now();

    let search = query
        .search
        .as_deref()
        .map(str::trim)
        .filter(|term| !term.is_empty());

    let mut rows = match search {
        Some(term) => {
            // Literal substring match: wildcards from the input are stripped
            // rather than interpreted.
            let pattern = format!("%{}%", term.replace(['%', '_'], " "));
            let sql = format!("{LIST_SQL_HEAD} WHERE u.email LIKE ?2{LIST_SQL_TAIL}");
            connection
                .query(sql, (now, pattern))
                .await
                .map_err(auth::internal)?
        }
        None => {
            let sql = format!("{LIST_SQL_HEAD}{LIST_SQL_TAIL}");
            connection
                .query(sql, [now])
                .await
                .map_err(auth::internal)?
        }
    };

    let mut users = Vec::new();
    while let Some(row) = rows.next().await.map_err(auth::internal)? {
        users.push(AdminUser {
            id: row.get(0).map_err(auth::internal)?,
            email: row.get(1).map_err(auth::internal)?,
            wallet: auth::nullable_text(&row, 2)?,
            created_at: row.get(3).map_err(auth::internal)?,
            sessions: row.get(4).map_err(auth::internal)?,
            codes: row.get(5).map_err(auth::internal)?,
        });
    }
    Ok(Json(users))
}

pub async fn delete_user(
    State(state): State<crate::AppState>,
    headers: HeaderMap,
    Path(id): Path<String>,
) -> ApiResult<Json<serde_json::Value>> {
    let admin = require_admin(&state.db, &headers).await?;
    if admin.id == id {
        return Err(ApiError::BadRequest(
            "You cannot delete your own account.".into(),
        ));
    }

    let connection = state.db.connect().map_err(auth::internal)?;
    // Children first — SQLite foreign keys are not guaranteed to be on.
    connection
        .execute("DELETE FROM sessions WHERE user_id = ?1", [id.as_str()])
        .await
        .map_err(auth::internal)?;
    connection
        .execute(
            "DELETE FROM discount_codes WHERE user_id = ?1",
            [id.as_str()],
        )
        .await
        .map_err(auth::internal)?;
    connection
        .execute(
            "DELETE FROM password_resets WHERE user_id = ?1",
            [id.as_str()],
        )
        .await
        .map_err(auth::internal)?;
    let removed = connection
        .execute("DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ?1", [id.as_str()])
        .await
        .map_err(auth::internal)?;

    if removed == 0 {
        return Err(ApiError::NotFound("No account with that id.".into()));
    }
    Ok(Json(serde_json::json!({ "ok": true })))
}

async fn scalar(connection: &libsql::Connection, sql: &str) -> ApiResult<i64> {
    let mut rows = connection.query(sql, ()).await.map_err(auth::internal)?;
    first_count(&mut rows).await
}

async fn first_count(rows: &mut libsql::Rows) -> ApiResult<i64> {
    match rows.next().await.map_err(auth::internal)? {
        Some(row) => Ok(row.get(0).map_err(auth::internal)?),
        None => Ok(0),
    }
}

useSeoMeta({ title: 'Admin — Payvand' })
definePageMeta({ middleware: 'auth' })

const { fetchStats, fetchUsers, deleteUser } = useAdminApi()

const stats = ref<AdminStats | null>(null)
const rows = ref<AdminUser[]>([])
const search = ref('')
const loading = ref(true)
const busy = ref(false)
const forbidden = ref(false)
const failure = ref('')

/** ofetch surfaces the HTTP status in one of several shapes. */
function statusOf(error: unknown): number | undefined {
  if (typeof error !== 'object' || error === null) return undefined
  const candidate = error as {
    status?: number
    statusCode?: number
    response?: { status?: number }
  }
  return candidate.status ?? candidate.statusCode ?? candidate.response?.status
}

async function load() {
  failure.value = ''
  loading.value = true
  try {
    stats.value = await fetchStats()
    rows.value = await fetchUsers(search.value.trim() || undefined)
    forbidden.value = false
  } catch (error) {
    if (statusOf(error) === 403) {
      forbidden.value = true
    } else {
      failure.value = apiErrorMessage(error, 'Could not load the admin data.')
    }
  } finally {
    loading.value = false
  }
}

async function searchNow() {
  await load()
}

async function remove(row: AdminUser) {
  const confirmed = window.confirm(
    `Delete ${row.email}?\n\nThis removes the account, its sessions, its discount codes and any pending reset links. This cannot be undone.`
  )
  if (!confirmed) return

  busy.value = true
  try {
    await deleteUser(row.id)
    await load()
  } catch (error) {
    failure.value = apiErrorMessage(error, 'Could not delete that account.')
  } finally {
    busy.value = false
  }
}

function formatDate(seconds: number): string {
  return new Date(seconds * 1000).toLocaleDateString()
}

onMounted(load)
</script>

The admin panel is built and fully verified locally. Summary:

## What you get

**`/admin` in the web app** — stats cards (accounts, live sessions, discount codes, pending resets), an account table with search showing each account's live sessions and discount codes, and a Delete button that removes an account **with everything it owns** (sessions, discount codes, pending reset links) behind a confirmation. That's also your probe-account cleanup from earlier, one click each.

**Three new endpoints** behind one gate:
- `GET /api/admin/stats`
- `GET /api/admin/users?search=…`
- `DELETE /api/admin/users/{id}`

## The key design choice

**Access is configuration, not schema**: the API matches the signed-in account's address against an `ADMIN_EMAILS` env var (comma-separated). No role column, no bootstrap chicken-and-egg — granting or revoking access is "edit the env, redeploy." Every admin call re-checks the session first (**401** if signed out) and then the address (**403** otherwise); the page renders a clear "no admin access" card on 403. Deleting your own account is refused (400) so you can't lock yourself out.

Supporting changes: `ApiError` gained `Forbidden` (403) and `NotFound` (404) variants, and the [admin module](apps/api/src/admin.rs) carries its own tests.

## Verified

- `cargo test`: **18/18** (new test covers the gate, stats, search, cascading delete, 404/400/self-delete, plus `ADMIN_EMAILS` parsing edge cases — the env var is owned by a single test to avoid process-global races) · **lint PASS** · **typecheck PASS**
- **Live end-to-end run** locally: no session → 401, non-admin → 403 (on both stats *and* delete), admin → 200 with correct counts, search narrows, delete → 200 → repeat 404 → self-delete 400.
- Docs updated: README endpoints, a new **Admin** section, env table row, and `.env.example`. Your local `apps/web/.env` now has `ADMIN_EMAILS` set to your address (written from the credentials file, value never displayed), so `/admin` works in local dev as soon as you sign in with that account.

+//! Admin API — platform oversight for the people running Payvand.
+//!
+//! Authorization is configuration, not schema: `ADMIN_EMAILS` (comma
+//! separated) is matched against the signed-in account's address, so
+//! granting access never needs a migration or a bootstrap row. Every
+//! handler re-checks the session first, then the address — a stolen
+//! response shape is useless without a live admin session.
+
+use axum::extract::{Json, Path, Query, State};
+use axum::http::HeaderMap;
+use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
+
+use crate::auth::{self, User};
+use crate::db::SharedDb;
+use crate::payments::{ApiError, ApiResult};
+
+/// True when the address is listed in `ADMIN_EMAILS`.
+/// Comparison happens on the normalized (trimmed, lowercased) form.
+pub fn is_admin(email: &str) -> bool {
+    std::env::var("ADMIN_EMAILS")
+        .map(|raw| {
+            raw.split(',')
+                .map(|entry| entry.trim().to_lowercase())
+                .any(|entry| !entry.is_empty() && entry == email)
+        })
+        .unwrap_or(false)
+}
+
+/// The signed-in account, when it has admin access.
+pub async fn require_admin(db: &SharedDb, headers: &HeaderMap) -> ApiResult<User> {
+    let user = auth::require_user(db, headers).await?;
+    if is_admin(&user.email) {
+        Ok(user)
+    } else {
+        Err(ApiError::Forbidden(
+            "This account does not have admin access.".into(),
+        ))
+    }
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
+pub struct Stats {
+    pub users: i64,
+    pub active_sessions: i64,
+    pub discount_codes: i64,
+    pub pending_resets: i64,
+}
+
+pub async fn stats(
+    State(state): State<crate::AppState>,
+    headers: HeaderMap,
+) -> ApiResult<Json<Stats>> {
+    require_admin(&state.db, &headers).await?;
+    let connection = state.db.connect().map_err(auth::internal)?;
+
+    Ok(Json(Stats {
+        users: scalar(&connection, "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users").await?,
+        active_sessions: {
+            let mut rows = connection
+                .query(
+                    "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions WHERE expires_at > ?1",
+                    [auth::unix_now()],
+                )
+                .await
+                .map_err(auth::internal)?;
+            first_count(&mut rows).await?
+        },
+        discount_codes: scalar(&connection, "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM discount_codes").await?,
+        pending_resets: scalar(&connection, "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM password_resets").await?,
+    }))
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
+pub struct UserListQuery {
+    pub search: Option<String>,
+}
+
+/// One row of the admin user table: the account plus what it currently
+/// holds (live sessions, discount codes).
+#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
+pub struct AdminUser {
+    pub id: String,
+    pub email: String,
+    pub wallet: Option<String>,
+    pub created_at: i64,
+    pub sessions: i64,
+    pub codes: i64,
+}
+
+const LIST_SQL_HEAD: &str = "SELECT u.id, u.email, u.wallet, u.created_at,
+        (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions s WHERE s.user_id = u.id AND s.expires_at > ?1),
+        (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM discount_codes d WHERE d.user_id = u.id)
+    FROM users u";
+const LIST_SQL_TAIL: &str = " ORDER BY u.created_at DESC LIMIT 200";
+
+pub async fn list_users(
+    State(state): State<crate::AppState>,
+    headers: HeaderMap,
+    Query(query): Query<UserListQuery>,
+) -> ApiResult<Json<Vec<AdminUser>>> {
+    require_admin(&state.db, &headers).await?;
+    let connection = state.db.connect().map_err(auth::internal)?;
+    let now = auth::unix_now();
+
+    let search = query
+        .search
+        .as_deref()
+        .map(str::trim)
+        .filter(|term| !term.is_empty());
+
+    let mut rows = match search {
+        Some(term) => {
+            // Literal substring match: wildcards from the input are stripped
+            // rather than interpreted.
+            let pattern = format!("%{}%", term.replace(['%', '_'], " "));
+            let sql = format!("{LIST_SQL_HEAD} WHERE u.email LIKE ?2{LIST_SQL_TAIL}");
+            connection
+                .query(&sql, (now, pattern))
+                .await
+                .map_err(auth::internal)?
+        }
+        None => {
+            let sql = format!("{LIST_SQL_HEAD}{LIST_SQL_TAIL}");
+            connection
+                .query(&sql, [now])
+                .await
+                .map_err(auth::internal)?
+        }
+    };
+
+    let mut users = Vec::new();
+    while let Some(row) = rows.next().await.map_err(auth::internal)? {
+        users.push(AdminUser {
+            id: row.get(0).map_err(auth::internal)?,
+            email: row.get(1).map_err(auth::internal)?,
+            wallet: auth::nullable_text(&row, 2)?,
+            created_at: row.get(3).map_err(auth::internal)?,
+            sessions: row.get(4).map_err(auth::internal)?,
+            codes: row.get(5).map_err(auth::internal)?,
+        });
+    }
+    Ok(Json(users))
+}
+
+pub async fn delete_user(
+    State(state): State<crate::AppState>,
+    headers: HeaderMap,
+    Path(id): Path<String>,
+) -> ApiResult<Json<serde_json::Value>> {
+    let admin = require_admin(&state.db, &headers).await?;
+    if admin.id == id {
+        return Err(ApiError::BadRequest(
+            "You cannot delete your own account.".into(),
+        ));
+    }
+
+    let connection = state.db.connect().map_err(auth::internal)?;
+    // Children first — SQLite foreign keys are not guaranteed to be on.
+    connection
+        .execute("DELETE FROM sessions WHERE user_id = ?1", [id.as_str()])
+        .await
+        .map_err(auth::internal)?;
+    connection
+        .execute(
+            "DELETE FROM discount_codes WHERE user_id = ?1",
+            [id.as_str()],
+        )
+        .await
+        .map_err(auth::internal)?;
+    connection
+        .execute(
+            "DELETE FROM password_resets WHERE user_id = ?1",
+            [id.as_str()],
+        )
+        .await
+        .map_err(auth::internal)?;
+    let removed = connection
+        .execute("DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ?1", [id.as_str()])
+        .await
+        .map_err(auth::internal)?;
+
+    if removed == 0 {
+        return Err(ApiError::NotFound("No account with that id.".into()));
+    }
+    Ok(Json(serde_json::json!({ "ok": true })))
+}
+
+async fn scalar(connection: &libsql::Connection, sql: &str) -> ApiResult<i64> {
+    let mut rows = connection.query(sql, ()).await.map_err(auth::internal)?;
+    first_count(&mut rows).await
+}
+
+async fn first_count(rows: &mut libsql::Rows) -> ApiResult<i64> {
+    match rows.next().await.map_err(auth::internal)? {
+        Some(row) => Ok(row.get(0).map_err(auth::internal)?),
+        None => Ok(0),
+    }
+}

+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests {

+export interface AdminStats {
+  users: number
+  active_sessions: number
+  discount_codes: number
+  pending_resets: number
+}
+
+export interface AdminUser {
+  id: string
+  email: string
+  wallet: string | null
+  created_at: number
+  sessions: number
+  codes: number
+}
+
+/**
+ * Admin endpoints. Access is decided by the API (`ADMIN_EMAILS`), not by
+ * the client — every call can still come back 403 and the page must handle
+ * that rather than assuming anything.
+ */
+export function useAdminApi() {
+  const config = useRuntimeConfig()
+  const base = config.public.apiBase
+  const { token } = useAuth()
+
+  function headers(): Record<string, string> {
+    return token.value ? { authorization: `Bearer ${token.value}` } : {}
+  }
+
+  async function fetchStats(): Promise<AdminStats> {
+    return await $fetch<AdminStats>(`${base}/api/admin/stats`, {
+      headers: headers()
+    })
+  }
+
+  async function fetchUsers(search?: string): Promise<AdminUser[]> {
+    return await $fetch<AdminUser[]>(`${base}/api/admin/users`, {
+      headers: headers(),
+      query: search ? { search } : {}
+    })
+  }
+
+  async function deleteUser(id: string): Promise<void> {
+    await $fetch(`${base}/api/admin/users/${id}`, {
+      method: 'DELETE',
+      headers: headers()
+    })
+  }
+
+  return { fetchStats, fetchUsers, deleteUser }
+}

## What you get

**`/admin` in the web app** — stats cards (accounts, live sessions, discount codes, pending resets), an account table with search showing each account's live sessions and discount codes, and a Delete button that removes an account **with everything it owns** (sessions, discount codes, pending reset links) behind a confirmation. **Three new endpoints** behind one gate:
- `GET /api/admin/stats`
- `GET /api/admin/users?search=…`
- `DELETE /api/admin/users/{id}`

## The key design choice

**Access is configuration, not schema**: the API matches the signed-in account's address against an `ADMIN_EMAILS` env var (comma-separated). No role column, no bootstrap chicken-and-egg — granting or revoking access is "edit the env, redeploy." Every admin call re-checks the session first (**401** if signed out) and then the address (**403** otherwise); the page renders a clear "no admin access" card on 403. Deleting your own account is refused (400) so you can't lock yourself out.

        }
    }

/// The pure part of the feed — newest first, capped, deterministic even
/// when several invoices share a second — so it is testable without a cluster.
fn shape_feed(mut records: Vec<PaymentRecord>, limit: usize) -> (Vec<AdminPayment>, usize) {
    let total = records.len();
    records.sort_by(|a, b| {
        b.created_at_unix
            .cmp(&a.created_at_unix)
            .then_with(|| b.settled_at_unix.cmp(&a.settled_at_unix))
            .then_with(|| a.id.cmp(&b.id))
    });
    records.truncate(limit);
    (
        records.into_iter().map(AdminPayment::from).collect(),
        total,
    )
}

+/// The pure part of the feed — newest first, capped, deterministic even
+/// when several invoices share a second — so it is testable without a cluster.
+fn shape_feed(mut records: Vec<PaymentRecord>, limit: usize) -> (Vec<AdminPayment>, usize) {
+    let total = records.len();
+    records.sort_by(|a, b| {
+        b.created_at_unix
+            .cmp(&a.created_at_unix)
+            .then_with(|| b.settled_at_unix.cmp(&a.settled_at_unix))
+            .then_with(|| a.id.cmp(&b.id))
+    });
+    records.truncate(limit);
+    (
+        records.into_iter().map(AdminPayment::from).collect(),
+        total,
+    )
+}

/** base58 for a byte array — Solana's encoding for signatures. */
export function base58Encode(bytes: Uint8Array): string {
  const alphabet = '123456789ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijkmnopqrstuvwxyz'
  let zeros = 0
  while (zeros < bytes.length && bytes[zeros] === 0) zeros++
  let value = 0n
  for (const byte of bytes) value = (value << 8n) | BigInt(byte)
  let out = ''
  while (value > 0n) {
    out = alphabet[Number(value % 58n)] + out
    value /= 58n
  }
  return '1'.repeat(zeros) + out
}

const BASE58_ALPHABET = '123456789ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijkmnopqrstuvwxyz'

/** Solana's base58 — the encoding the API expects signatures in. */
export function base58Encode(bytes: Uint8Array): string {
  let zeros = 0
  while (zeros < bytes.length && bytes[zeros] === 0) zeros++
  let value = 0n
  for (const byte of bytes) value = (value << 8n) | BigInt(byte)
  let out = ''
  while (value > 0n) {

    value /= 58n
  }
  return '1'.repeat(zeros) + out

The profile experience is built, tested, and live. Committed as `28de7d3`, pushed, both projects deployed (the flaky network ate two deploys first; retries went through).

## What you got

**`/profile` page** (linked from the header and mobile menu) with three cards:

1. **Wallet** — connect with the usual wallet buttons, then one "Link this wallet" button: the API issues an exact message, the wallet signs it, and the address attaches to your account. Shows the linked address with a "Linked" badge.
2. **Monthly allowance** — if none exists, a prominent prompt explains the one-signature setup and links to the budget page (your "prompted to set a monthly allowance"). If one exists: monthly limit, spent this month, **remaining** with a progress bar, pot available, and a Manage button.
3. **Transactions** — every payment involving your wallet: direction arrows (green in / red out), amount, memo, counterparty, date, status badge, plus a Refresh button.

**Sign in with wallet** — `/signin` now has an "or" section: connect the wallet, press one button, sign the challenge, you're in. If the wallet isn't linked yet, the API says so and points back to email sign-in.

## The design decisions worth knowing

- **Challenge/response auth**: the server stores the exact message (one live challenge per address, 5-minute expiry, single use), verifies the base58 signature strictly against the address, and checks the **purpose** — a signature made for signing in can never be reused to link, or vice versa. `users.wallet` got a partial unique index, so a wallet belongs to at most one account.
- **Silent payments appear in your history**: the program records the *session key* as payer for budget payments, so the transactions endpoint also scans budget accounts to map a buyer's session key back to them — payments you made without any popup still show as "sent".
- Linking only proves ownership; the link endpoint always re-checks your session first.

## Verified

- `cargo test` **21/21** (3 new: full link→signin flow with a real ed25519 key, wrong-key rejection, replay rejection, purpose mismatch, expired challenge, unlinked-wallet refusal, transactions gates, plus the direction-matching unit test) · **lint 0** · **typecheck 0**
- Local HTTP smoke: challenge issues correct text, bad signature → 400, anonymous → 401, all routes registered
- Production: challenge → **200** (proves the `wallet_challenges` migration ran against Turso), wrong-purpose → **400** with the right message, anonymous link/transactions → **401**, `/profile` → **302** to `/signin?next=/profile`, `/signin` renders with the wallet section
